Turn 1 is free (cubes charge, punch defends): put permanent Strength online, then pour all damage into one cube, blocking each incoming round, and keep enough HP for the elite ahead.
Survive first: block on every attack turn, take no unnecessary damage; use the free WINDUP turn to grow Strength, then grind 320 HP down over cleave cycles while staying above the next hit.
Single weak scaling hallway fight: frontload damage and kill within about three turns, blocking the 8-damage hits only as needed to stay near 90% HP for the act boss.
Short two-target hallway fight: frontload damage and delete both toadpoles in the first two turns, blocking only what is needed, to keep HP near 90% for the act boss.
Kill the backup-calling rat first, then the 8-damage rat, then the last. Frontload damage with heavy single hits, blocking only the incoming 14 while the board shrinks.

Focus one gardener at a time (lowest HP, biggest attack) to cut attackers fast; burst each target with the highest-damage cards before Skittish block matters; block only lethal hits, accept some HP loss to end this in ~5 turns.
Single 58 HP worm at full HP: end it fast with attacks, blocking only the 11-damage Acid Goop turns, and use Breakthrough when adds appear. Keep HP near full for the act boss run.

Full HP, no scaling in deck: burn the parasite down fast, using its no-damage INFECT turn freely; once 4 worms split, kill them quickly with AOE and focus, blocking LASH turns to stay healthy for the boss.

The parasite is dead; four stunned worms remain. Use the free turn for maximum damage, AOE first and finish lowest-HP worms so fewer attackers survive; then trim their bites while preserving HP for the act boss.
Use the free sleep/wake turns for full damage, then keep damage high while blocking enough to survive; it scales +10 Strength and we have none, so a long fight loses. Single target, no AOE priority.
Kill the Jaxfruit first to stop its buffs, then the Strangler before Constrict grinds us down; block only enough to survive and reach the coming rest site.
Single 70 HP construct that scales each cycle: burn it down before buffs stack, block only the heavy turns, and keep enough HP for the boss three floors away.

No permanent Strength here: this is a damage race with limited blocking. Use the two free buff turns for maximum damage, break 150 HP for the stun, then block the big PLOW/STOMP hits while racing its ramp.
Kill the nectar first so its buff never becomes repeated 18-damage turns; use the rock's free stunned turn for full damage, then finish the rock. Keep HP above ~50%.
Kill fast, do not turtle: AOE all three and focus them down one at a time so fewer attackers stay alive. No scaling needed in this short hallway; end it in a few turns and keep HP for Kaiser Crab.
All damage goes to the Ovicopter body: its death removes the eggs, so never spend attacks on eggs or larvae. Block just enough for the 19 SMASH, keep HP above the boss line, and end this fight fast.
AOE all three down fast while blocking the big hits; nectar first, then rock, then silk. Never eat two unblocked attacks; this fight must end in a few turns.
Trade a little HP for damage to end this in ~3 turns: keep HP near the 85% boss-prep line while killing the Nibbit before its buff/attack cycle grinds us down.
Race this down in about 3 turns: focus the low-HP buffing Jaxfruit first, then the Strangler, spending a bit of HP on damage if needed to stop the buffs and Constrict from stacking.

Maximize damage every turn and end this in about four turns: drop Inflame+ early, apply vulnerable, stack Breakthrough/Hemokinesis/Strikes. Only block when a hit would otherwise drop us badly; HP is traded for speed, not saved.
Focus everything on Fogmog itself; the summoned add is temporary or caught by AOE. Roughly four turns of damage, block the big hits, keep enough HP for the rest site and Vantom.

Spend the cheap opening turns (7-damage hit, Prepare) on permanent powers first, strip the 9 Slippery with multi-hit attacks, save real block for the Dismember turns, then kill the 183 HP boss inside ~7 turns.
Race the Tunneler down in about 3 turns: use strength and multi-hit damage to break or outpace its burrow block, don't settle into pure blocking, and keep both potions for the act boss.
Burst the Nectar bowlbug first before it buffs and hits for 18, using AOE to chip both; block the incoming headbutts and finish the Rock while it is stunned. Fight should end in about four turns.

Use the free debuff turn to land a big damage chunk and let permanent Strength come online, then hold full damage pressure while blocking just enough for the telegraphed 17-21; finish within about five turns.
Focus one Chomper down while AOE chips both, blocking each Clamp every turn; fewer attackers is the defence. Debuffs need two hits through Artifact 2.
Open with permanent Strength powers (they do not feed Vital Spark), then attack-heavy: few skill plays, block only the big hits, kill in about four turns, keep HP for the boss.
Burn down one Toadpole at a time to cut incoming damage, blocking the weaker attack as needed; keep the HP loss small since the Waterfall Giant boss is the real clock.
Single weak hallway enemy with mild scaling: apply Vulnerable and burst it down within about three turns, blocking the 12-damage SLAM hits, so the 44 HP pool stays healthy for the act boss.
Single 51 HP thief with light self-buffing: burst it down in about two turns with the big attacks, blocking only what is cheap, so HP and gold stay intact for the boss clock.
End this quickly: concentrate all damage on one slug at a time so incoming damage drops each kill, blocking only what is cheap; no long-term scaling plays until the board thins.

Full HP versus one 60 HP enemy: end it fast with frontloaded damage, take Inflame early, block only what prevents real HP loss, and keep HP and potions for the coming elite-free path to the Waterfall Giant boss.
Single 67 HP enemy: burn it down quickly with frontloaded damage while blocking the 12-13 hits, so status cards don't clog the deck ahead of the boss. Keep potions in reserve.
Short 3-enemy hallway: drop rats one at a time (biggest attacker first) so incoming shrinks each turn, accept only chip damage, and keep HP and potions intact for the waterfall giant boss.

Use the free opening Buff turn to land permanent Strength and start scaling, then push ~30 damage/turn so it dies near turn 10. Bank block for Pressure Gun, keep HP above the steam stacks, and fully block the self-destruct turn.
Kill the hopper inside its escape clock: full damage every turn, permanent Strength early, just enough block to survive the 17-21 hits. The fight ends too fast to matter otherwise.
Race one 92 HP enemy: push damage every turn, land vulnerable early to amplify frontload, and break the 32 burrow block within a turn or two so the fight ends before repeated 23s drain 45 HP.

One non-scaling 126 HP hunter: frontload damage with vulnerable to end it in a few turns, while blocking the 17-21 attacks enough to keep HP near the boss-prep target and limit cards played under goop.
Push maximum damage from turn one, land permanent Strength on safe turns, keep enough block for the 3x7/18-21 attacks, and finish in about five turns before Dazes clog the deck.
Three bugs: cut attacker count fast. Kill Nectar (buffs, 18 next) and Rock; Egg is cheap/AOE fodder. Block the big hits, keep HP near 85% for Knowledge Demon, land Strength only when safe.
Block the big hits first, damage only with spare energy; land permanent strength only on turns the incoming attack is covered; finish it before its strength stacks.
Short single-enemy fight: end it fast with attacks and Panache procs, blocking only the 13-damage Stomp turn. Avoid unnecessary HP loss; the run needs HP for the Kin boss.
59 HP single enemy that buffs itself: frontload damage and end it in about three turns, blocking only enough to limit chip damage; keep potions for the act boss.
Damage race: it wakes buffed and hits 23 a turn while our block is thin, so pour damage into it and finish before HP runs out; the sleep turn is free setup.
Race the pair down: focus the attacking Flyconid first to stop its hits and spores, then finish the buffing Jaxfruit. Block enough to avoid real HP loss and keep HP for the act boss.

Short 3-on-1 brawl: use AOE and multi-hit attacks to strip Slippery and drop all three Inklets in ~2-3 turns, blocking only cheaply since incoming is small and our HP is 61%. No scaling enemy here — pure damage ends it safely.
Race them down: focus the strangler first so Constrict stops ticking, sweep the jaxfruit with multi-target damage, and spend only the block needed to survive the big hits.
Single summoner: burst Fogmog now while its Summon turn deals no damage, then block HEADBUTT/SWIPE enough to finish; keep HP for the boss 3 floors away.
Play the permanent Strength power in the opening turns, then focus every single-target attack on the Priest; AOE clears the followers incidentally. Keep enough block for the beam turns.
Single 45 HP monster that grows each buff cycle. Deal damage every turn and end it in about three turns, blocking only what is needed to stay near full HP for the coming elites and boss.
Three weak, non-scaling attackers. Focus damage to remove the medium slime (biggest hit plus status), then clear the small ones; block only what is needed and end the fight within ~3 turns.

Race it down: it only has 90 HP but scales every turn. Full damage each turn, block only enough to survive the incoming hit, accept small HP loss to end it fast; run_plan's reserved potions stay for the boss.
Focus one low-HP Nibbit down at a time to halve incoming damage, blocking the big attack turns; accept small chip damage to shorten the fight before HISS buffs pile up.
Focus the 28 HP slime first to halve incoming, block the 11-13 hits with block cards and skills, then finish Flyconid; accept only small HP leaks and end near boss-entry HP.
Single non-scaling 64 HP monster: burst it down in two to three turns. Block only the bigger hits so HP stays near 90% for the rest site and The Kin fight; no long-term value here.
Single 92 HP tunneler that grows into 23-per-turn hits. Push damage every turn, including through its burrow block, blocking only enough to stay healthy for the act boss.

Only 72 total HP and no scaling: kill the 24 HP egg first to halve attacker count, then focus the Rock. Block efficiently to trigger its Imbalanced stun; no potions, they are reserved for Kaiser Crab.
One 140 HP scaling elite: use the free non-attacking first turn to set up permanent growth, then full damage every turn, blocking the Pounce hits; finish it before the second Pounce.
Rush the Ovicopter: 131 HP, no scaling of its own, and its eggs vanish when it dies. Kill within about four turns so summons never stack, blocking the 19 SMASH, to keep HP near the boss-prep target.
Focus fire one Chomper down to halve incoming damage, then finish the second. Block the clamps, trade a little HP for speed since a rest site follows and the deck clearly outclasses them.
Spread damage across all three segments to keep HP totals close, block the big multi-hits, then finish all three in the same turn (AoE + multi-hit); never commit to killing one segment alone.
Block every turn, use the early lighter turns for permanent Strength, keep both claws' HP aligned (hourglass ticks both), then burst both down in the same turn.
Only one 48 HP enemy: push damage every turn, use vulnerable and the AOE to shorten the fight to ~3 turns, and block just enough to keep HP high for the act boss; do not spend turns on pure setup.
Cultists scale each turn, so end it quickly: remove the harder hitter first, keep enough block that 44 HP cannot be chipped away, but keep damage the priority.

Kill attackers one by one: each kill stuns the survivors, turning kills into free turns. Use AOE and vulnerability for damage, block only what is needed, keep HP near 85% for the boss and hold the reserved potion.
Short single-enemy fight. Push damage, block its 12-14 attacks fully to deny Strength stacking, and keep HP near 85% for the Waterfall Giant boss in 3 floors.
Wipe the rats fast with AOE and hourglass chip before backup arrives; block only the residual hit, keep HP near 85% for the Waterfall Giant boss.
Deal ~25/turn to kill by T10-11 while fully blocking Pressure Gun and Stomp; never let HP fall below the steam-stack number, and hold enough block for the final explosion turn.
Single 84 HP enemy on a 4-turn escape clock that steals cards. Race it down at roughly 21+ damage per turn, blocking the biggest attacks to stay safe.
Burst the Tunneler down before its 32 retained block comes up: heavy damage now, block only the 13 bite, and break any block it gains within the same turn.

Push ~25+ damage per turn on the single 140 HP elite, spending block mainly on the POUNCE turns so Strength never outgrows our defence; end it in about five turns while HP stays banked for the act boss.

Clear both bowlbugs during the beetle's 3 sleep turns, fully blocking the Stone bug's 15 to stun it and eating the Silk bug's poison debuff; then focus the woken beetle with Vulnerable and our best damage, keeping enough block for its esca…
Turn 1 is free: put everything into the Obscura, then race it down in ~4 turns while blocking the largest hits; the illusion revives if killed and vanishes when the Obscura dies.
At 17 HP block to survive each turn first, damage second. Kill the Rock (biggest hit) then the Egg (24 HP) to cut incoming fast; keep Strength/block potions for the boss.
Everything goes into the Ovicopter body: when it dies the eggs vanish. Block just enough to survive each hit, then push damage — never attack eggs.

Focus all damage into a single Chomper so only one 16-damage clamp remains, blocking each clamping turn just enough to survive; do not count on debuffs before Artifact is stripped, and finish the second quickly.

Race the sandpit: maximum damage into the boss each turn, blocking only enough to survive. Extend the clock whenever an extra-turn effect is affordable; with the fight extended several turns, permanent Strength is worth an early turn.
41 HP single hallway enemy that does not scale hard: kill within about three turns with Bash/Setup Strike damage, blocking only the bigger SLAM turns so HP loss stays small.
Race the eel down before its CRASH/THRASH grind kills us at 41 HP: push damage to trigger the 75 HP stun, use that free turn, keep enough block for the 99-Vulnerable follow-up, end it fast.
Cheap, quick clear: both enemies die to a couple of AOE hits, so spend only what finishes them this fight and save HP and powers for the boss.
Punch through the clam's decaying Plating with strength-boosted attacks, using its non-attacking PRESSURIZE turn for scaling; block the 10–13 hits and stay high before the boss.
Play permanent Strength early while blocking the big hits; cross the 50% stun line to cancel an attack, then burst the Eel down fast, because after the stun we are Vulnerable.
Sweep all three with AOE; deaths stun the survivors, so chaining kills is both damage and defence. End it in two or three turns, keeping HP for the boss.

Use the sleep turns for permanent Strength and block, never breaking the boss's Plating early; once awake, burst with Strength-boosted attacks and AOE while blocking the 19 and 11x2 hits before Soul Siphon lands.
Apply permanent strength early, then burst with AOE and attacks; punch through the 32 burrow block within a turn or two so the 23s stop. Block only the hits that actually cost HP.
Block the combined incoming every turn, use cheap AOE to sweep the egg and chip the rock, finish the 15-damage rock first; spend no resources, keep HP for Kaiser Crab.
End it in a few turns: concentrate damage to remove one enemy quickly, use strength plus AOE to sweep both, block the clamps and keep HP above lethal.
Cover nearly all of every attack turn with few big block cards, chip with spare energy; use the zero-damage goop turn for permanent Strength and full damage. Survive to the crab boss.

Short single-target fight on floor 4: burst the Sea Punk down in about three turns, set vulnerable before heavy hits, and block only enough to keep HP loss small for the boss climb. No potions needed here.

Single clam with 58 HP and decaying Plating: burst it down in ~3-4 turns, using multi-hits/heavy attacks to punch through block, while blocking the 10-13 hits enough to survive the floor with boss-ready HP.
Single 52 HP monster with no growth: race it down in about 3 turns, blocking only enough to cap HP loss, so it swings as few times as possible.

56 HP single enemy that grows on unblocked damage: end it in about 3 turns with frontload attacks, but block its LASH/TACKLE fully so it never stacks Strength. No potions; save HP and both potions for the resting site and the sleeping boss.
Do not break sleep early; use sleeping turns for powers and block, then burst the boss down once it wakes, still blocking its attack turns — faster kill means fewer Soul Siphons and less HP lost.
Single 92 HP Tunneler: push damage hard from turn one, break the 32 burrow block in one or two turns, accept some chip damage to end it in about 3-4 turns.
Kill within four turns before it escapes with a stolen card: frontload damage, take the free no-attack turn to burst, and cover the 21-damage turn since HP is low.
Attack-heavy race: minimize skills so it does not scale, dump attacks and Fiend Fire, block only on the biggest incoming turns, finish within a few turns.

Funnel all damage into the 129 HP Obscura, it dies and the minion leaves too; only swat the minion in one blow when that stops a lethal combined hit. Keep HP and the reserved potion for the act boss in 3 floors.
Boss heals and grows stronger every cycle, so end it fast: use the no-attack curse turns for scaling and block, then push maximum damage; never let a 30-36 turn land unblocked.

Race the sculptor: turn 1 is a free window, frontload all damage and powers, then keep max damage every turn to kill within about 4 turns; only block with spare energy when a kill line is not available.
Both enemies die in one or two hits each, so end it fast: clear the buffing toadpole first, let AOE hit both, block only the 7 attack, and don't spend potions.
Low-HP group fight: use AOE and every attack to clear slugs fast, taking the stun windows from kills as free defence; block just enough that HP stays near target for the act boss.

Short brawl: burst all three rats down before the summoner adds more, using AOE on the group; give priority to the rat calling for backup, block only the cheap damage, and keep HP above the boss-prep target.
Single 51-HP merc: burst it down within two to three turns, blocking the 8x2 attack while doing so, then take the rest site; keep potions and HP for the boss.
Deal maximum damage from turn one so it dies near T8-10, keeping the death explosion small; block the escalating gun and the explosion enough to stay above the steam count.

Focus fire one Toadpole at a time, starting with the buffing one, using Bash's vulnerable to speed the kill; kill the second straight after, blocking only what is cheap. Two dead enemies end all incoming damage.
One 41 HP hallway enemy that buffs if ignored: end it fast, block only enough on its attack turns to stay safe, and keep HP for the upcoming elite/boss.
One hallway enemy that buffs and hits ~16 a turn: take it down in about three turns, blocking just enough to stay near full HP for the Waterfall Giant entry target.

One clam with decaying plating: push steady damage into it every turn, blocking the JET hits, and end it in a few turns before buffed JETs stack up — HP is needed above the boss self-destruct threshold.
Single non-scaling hallway enemy with tiny hits: push steady damage and end it in a few turns, blocking the small attacks, keeping HP near the boss target.
Remove the scaling cultist first before its Ritual snowballs, blocking just enough of both attackers' hits to reach the boss HP target, then finish the Seapunk.

Sprint the boss down before eruption stacks exceed our HP: push steady damage every turn, block pressure guns fully, spend self-damage engine to close the damage gap, and keep HP margin for the final explosion.
Two low-HP attackers, so end it fast: AOE and self-damage hit both, remove the 23-HP egg first to cut chip damage, then focus the rock, blocking its headbutt completely to stun it when cheap.
Kill the tunneler quickly: push full frontload now and through the burrow block so it never grinds us at 23 a turn. Block only enough to survive the bite, keep HP high for the act boss.
Ignore the eggs entirely and dump all damage into the Ovicopter, using AOE only as it incidentally hits the body: once the parent dies all its eggs vanish, which ends the extra incoming.
Keep all three segments' HP even and kill them in the same turn so none reattaches (25 HP). AOE and self-damage triggers hit all three; block the escalating hits, keep HP for the boss.

Four-body hallway: reduce attacker count fast, spreading area damage and multi-hit attacks (each hit caps at 9), taking down the lowest-HP/highest-damage bug first while blocking the rest; keep HP for the boss run.
Free debuff turn: set up powers and the self-damage engine, then kill within about four turns; block the 21/17 hits, accept small self-damage, keep HP for the boss and rest stop.

Race the sandpit: squeeze maximum damage every turn through the self-damage engine, extend the clock whenever a turn-extension card is affordable, and keep only enough block to survive the 18-29 hits.
Three low-HP slimes: burst them down one by one so total incoming drops fast, accepting only a few points of chip damage; no powers needed, keep HP near full ahead of the act boss.
Low-HP trio, deck has strong frontload: kill one raider per turn, assassin first (steady 10), then crossbow before its 14 shot, brute last; block only what is needed, AOE hits everything.
Burst the parasite down fast while its attacks are still small, then use AOE to sweep the worms before their Strength and Infection stack up; block only enough to survive a 16 hit.
All worms are stunned now: use the free window and AOE to hit all four, focusing lowest-HP worms one by one to cut attacker count. Block only enough to survive the bites.
Single 70 HP construct charges before attacking: use the free turns for maximum frontload and kill it in ~4 turns, blocking only when its attacks land; stay high for the act boss.
Short trio fight: burn each inklet's Slippery with cheap hits and AOE, then finish them one by one to cut incoming fast; frontload over blocking since HP is healthy and a rest site follows.
No scaling cards in deck, so race the priest: every single-target hit on it, AOE splashes the followers, and keep enough block for beam turns so chip damage plus debuffs don't grind us out.

Short hallway trio: hard cap of 9 per hit means multi-hit and AOE (hit all three) are the efficient damage; drop the buffing bug first so no Strength stacks, then the 8-attacker. Block only the blockable intents, HP loss kept small since t…
Hallway escape fight before the act boss: dump frontload damage (multi-hit/AOE cheap attacks) to kill it inside 4 turns, blocking just enough to stay healthy for the Worms boss.

T1 summon turn is free: frontload all single-target damage into Obscura (multi-hit and AOE welcome), expect it dead in ~3 turns so Parafright vanishes. Block only what is needed; do not waste damage on the illusion.
Two-myte hallway with high HP: end it in a few turns, taking the myte whose next move is the big bite first; frontload now while intents are light, stay healthy for the boss.

Clock fight, not an HP fight: push maximum damage every turn, take the buff turn as a free window. Play Frantic Escape whenever affordable rather than saving it for a low sandpit count, and only block enough to stay above the incoming atta…
Single enemy scaling every turn; race it with frontload damage, using the free first turn. Kill in about four turns, blocking only against the current hit — no slow setup.
Kill fast, blocking hits that would go unblocked to save max HP: focus the buffing scroll, then the 14-damage scroll, then the 5x2 scroll.
Long 281 HP hallway: full damage pressure to end it in ~6 turns, fully block the 20 and 33 attack turns, exploit buff/status turns to set up, keep HP for the Test Subject boss.
Kill both Toadpoles quickly, starting with the buffing one: dump big single-target hits, block only what is needed, and end the fight in about two turns.
Block the small hits fully each turn, spend leftover energy on damage and vulnerability; keep HP near full for Lagavulin and accept a slower, safer kill.
Burst the lone 51 HP gremlin: damage over blocking, block only with spare energy, end it within two to three turns so it barely buffs or steals.
Damage-first: race it under 75 HP to trigger the stun, then spend that window and the following turns finishing it; keep Defends for the big CRASH hits and stay near full HP for Lagavulin.
Block the 12-13 attacks fully each turn, spend leftover energy on steady damage, kill the 67 HP ship without trading HP, and arrive at the act boss healthy.
Block the ~14 incoming every turn and spend only leftover energy on damage; take the screeching debuffer first, then the other two, ending this in about three turns before the rest site.

Use the sleep turns to set up powers and stack block without waking it, chipping only into its plating. After the stun, block the 21 and 11x2 hits and kill before repeated drains gut our damage and block.

Both toadpoles sit at ~22 HP, so self-damage AoE (Inferno/Breakthrough) clears both within 2-3 turns. Take a few points of damage to kill fast rather than turtling; keep total HP loss small since the act boss still lies ahead.
Open with permanent scaling while the cultist wastes a buff turn, then burst the cultist down before its strikes grow; block the seapunk's hits and avoid needless self-damage HP loss.
Race it down to the 75-HP stun line fast; use the free stunned turn for scaling/block, then block hard through the 99 Vulnerable and finish before CRASH buffs stack up.
Single 55 HP enemy that grows stronger each time it lands unblocked damage. Race it down in about two to three turns while covering most of each incoming attack; end it before Strength stacks.
Single 51 HP enemy with a Strength buff next turn: end it in about two turns, trading a little HP for damage. Block only enough to stay safe from the 8x2, then dump damage; no reserve potions here.

Spend the sleep turns on powers and block, never breaking its Plating to wake it. After the wake stun, burst with Strength attacks, then block the 19 and 11x2 while killing before Soul Siphon drains us.
Kill the rock bug first; its headbutt stuns when fully blocked, so block it. AOE both bugs, then finish the 24-HP egg. Short fight; keep HP for the boss gap.

End it within two or three turns with all-out frontload damage, including AOE and self-damage triggers, before BURROW's persistent 32 block starts; hold just enough block for the 13 bite, never turtle into its block.
Ignore the Parafright: it revives, and it disappears when The Obscura dies; all damage goes to The Obscura. Block the combined incoming and finish near turn 4.
Single 121 HP toad with a free buff turn now: dump maximum damage this turn, then block the 23 and 17 attack turns and finish it within 3-4 turns; avoid multi-hit attacks once Thorns are up.
Set Strength powers early while blocking the multi-hit turns; self-damage procs AOE. Then finish fast, limiting small hits that add Dazed. Keep HP and potions for the boss.
Block every turn to survive; use self-damage only when fully safe; scale Strength with Rupture/Inflame and kill before the enemy outpaces our block.

Race the pack down with AOE and self-damage triggers so each HP-loss event also hits every enemy; block the incoming each turn and focus-fire the weakest so attackers drop fast; carry enough HP into the coming rest site.
No potions, 31 HP: use the no-attack curse turn to land Rupture/Inferno, keep self-damage tiny, fully block the 19/30-36 turns, and let permanent Strength ramp win the long grind.
Short two-enemy fight: frontload damage and AOE, killing one slug stuns the other for a turn and cuts incoming. Keep the power potion and most HP for the act boss.
Single 53 HP merc that buffs itself and steals gold per attack. Frontload damage to end it in a few turns; next node is a rest site, so a little HP loss is acceptable.
A 58 HP single enemy with 9 plating: chip damage is wasted, so frontload damage and burst it down in a few turns, blocking the 10-13 hits with leftover energy rather than grinding.

Focus-fire one gardener down at a time, breaking its first-hit block with the smallest hit before heavy hits; multi-hit/AOE damage is efficient. Kill fast, keep HP above the 85% boss line, no optional risk.

Land ~20 damage every turn to beat Hardened Shell in about four turns, but block most of each 14–18 hit: survive at 44 HP rather than trading, since the next node is a rest and the boss still needs HP and the potion.
Use sleep turns for powers/block while staying under 12 Plating, then race: full damage each wake cycle, cover the 19 and 11x2 hits, spend HP toward ~50% and let potions close the ~5/turn gap.
Two ~22-25 HP toadpoles that buff Spikes. Focus one down at a time, ignore its spikes' HP tax where block matters more, block only the 7-9 hits, and end the fight before Spikes pile up.
Grind through the 20/turn damage cap: deal about 20 each turn to end it near turn 4-5, block the 14-18 attacks meanwhile, play lasting defense early, and keep HP near full for the Soul Fysh boss.
One 82 HP enemy, low per-turn damage. Push attacks into vulnerability, block the hits that matter, and finish it before the gas debuffs clog the deck.

Focus-fire one ghost at a time so the count drops fast; small hits first, then the big multi-hit/AOE blows to punch through the per-turn first-hit block. End it before ENLARGE makes the total incoming lethal.

Focus the buffing cultist down first, then Seapunk; trade only the small chip damage, block just enough for the 11-attack, and end the fight within a few turns so the rest site and boss entry HP stay safe.
Push damage to end this before Beckons clog the deck; exhaust Beckons instead of holding them, block the large De Gas/Scream turns, and hold big attacks for non-intangible turns.
Focus one bug at a time so attackers drop fast; Hard to Kill caps each hit at 9, so multi-hit and per-turn Strength are efficient; end it in a few turns and keep HP loss small.
Kill the hopper within four turns, trading some HP for damage; block only enough to stay safely above 17 per turn, and end it before it escapes with a stolen card.

End this elite fast: concentrate everything on the Entomancer, favour fewer big hits over many small ones to limit Daze, block the Bees/Spear turns enough to keep HP near the ~68 boss-entry target. No potion.
Focus one Chomper down fast to halve incoming, blocking each Clamp; strip Artifact before debuffing. Expect a 3-4 turn fight: protect HP for the boss and keep the reserved potion.

Build powers and slow Strength early, especially on non-attacking curse turns; then trade damage and block evenly, using multi-hit and Vulnerable attacks, to out-pace the periodic 30 HP heal before its Strength stacks up.

Race the scrolls down with AOE and multi-hit before MORE_TEETH raises CHEW; block as much as possible since unblocked damage costs permanent max HP, not just health. Keep some HP for the forced elites and boss after this.

Single scaling hallway enemy at full HP: use the free buff turn to deal damage and set up in-turn Strength, then keep maximum damage every turn and end it in roughly four turns before Savage outgrows blocking.
Burst this elite down in a few turns: exhaust engine (Baking Gloves strength, Feel No Pain block) plus multi-hit attacks outpace it, so trade a little HP to end it before weak/vulnerable stack up.

Short two-enemy fight: focus damage to kill one slug quickly (its death stuns the other for a free turn), then finish the survivor; block only to avoid heavy chip, spend HP for tempo since we are at full health before the boss climb.
Kill the 47 HP Sea Punk in about 3 turns: attack each turn, block only the biggest hits, spend no potions and keep HP near the 90% boss-entry target.
Three frail rats that can summon reinforcements: end this in about two turns with area damage, blocking only where cheap. HP trade is fine here, but keep potions for the act boss.
Single 58 HP clam. Get permanent Strength online early, then push one large vulnerable hit per turn through its shrinking Plating; block only the JET hits needed to keep HP near 90% for the boss.
Short fight: get permanent Strength online early, exploit vulnerability, finish within ~3 turns; block every hit fully so its Strength never grows.
Total 84 HP across three frail slugs. Push AOE and permanent Strength early, kill as fast as possible; each kill stuns the others that turn, so damage doubles as defence. Block only the large hits.
Turn one is free: set up the power, then race the Beckon clock — clear Beckons before they cost HP, burst on non-Intangible turns, and hold nothing back late.
One 92 HP Tunneler: keep attacking every turn and break the 32 Burrow block within about two turns; block the 13/23 hits only after the block is down, holding HP for the boss.
Spread AOE and multi-hit across all three; finish the buffing lowest-HP bug first to stop group scaling. End in ~3 turns with HP loss small for the boss.
Use the free debuff turn to bring permanent Strength online, then kill within ~4 turns: block the 17/21 hits, apply vulnerable, land multi-hit burst, don't grind — HP is kept for the boss.

Frontload everything into the Ovicopter body and ignore the eggs — they vanish when it dies. Take the free summon turn to set up Strength, then block only what SMASH 19 requires while keeping HP toward the boss-entry target.

End it in ~3 turns: burst all three with AOE and Vulnerable, directed damage on the scaling Nectar then Rock, Egg dies incidentally. Block only the worst swings; never trade HP into the buffed-thrash turn.
Use the free no-attack first turn to bring powers online, then kill quickly through Vulnerable while blocking the 23/17 turns and limiting thorns chip. Keep HP for the boss after the forced rest.

Race the sandpit clock: damage first every turn, ramp permanent Strength plus Vulnerable, then multi-hit and AOE burst. Take every turn-extension the boss offers as soon as possible; block only lethal-size hits.
End the fight in about 3 turns: focus the medium leaf slime (status source, 35 HP) first, small slimes (11/13 HP) fall to spare damage. Trade a little chip HP for speed.
Fight ends in ~4 turns; race it: vulnerable early, multi-hit and heavy attacks up front, block only the 16-damage hit. Speed is the best HP defence before Vantom (85% entry target).
Two ~45 HP Nibbits, one buffing: end the fight fast, killing the buffing one first, then the other. Trade only small HP, since run wants ~85% HP entering Vantom in 8 floors.
Short hallway fight: burn the Flyconid first while blocking its heavy hits, then clear the slime fast before its status cards clog the deck. Keep potions for Vantom.
Race the 76-HP Mawler down in ~3–4 turns; block only ahead of the 18-damage swing, use separate small-attack turns for offense. Stay near 85% HP and keep the potion for Vantom.
Kill the main body fast; the summon dies with its parent, so don't chase it. Block the heavy HEADBUTT turns, use self-damage/Pyre to ramp, keep HP near the boss line.
Use the light first turns to play powers and stack permanent Strength, break the 9 Slippery layers with multi-hit attacks, fully block the Dismember turns, and burst on Prepare turns.

End this hallway fast: kill the honey Bowlbug before it finishes buffing into 18-damage Thrashes, block Rock's Headbutt completely to stun it, and don't overpay HP for scaling that this short fight won't use.
Race: all damage, break the 32 burrow block within a turn or two, then kill. Block just enough to survive the 23s; treat the burrow's 0-damage turn as a free attack turn.

Ramp permanent Strength in the early turns while only blocking what is lethal, then kill as fast as possible with multi-hit attacks; keep Skill plays per turn low since each one empowers its attacks, and end the fight before our HP runs ou…
End the fight in about three turns: focus one Toadpole down so AOE finishes both, block only what is needed. HP 67/86 — accept small losses, avoid letting buffs stack.
Focus one slug down fast: its death stuns the other for a free turn and halves incoming. Favour AOE/self-damage synergy, block only survivors, keep HP near full for the act boss.
Short fight: clear all three rats quickly with AOE and self-damage triggers, focusing the biggest attacker so no rat survives to call backup; block only enough to blunt the current hit.
Single 55 HP enemy: burst it down in about three turns instead of grinding, keeping enough block for its 12–14 hits. Ending it fast stops the Strength growth and preserves HP for the boss.
Use the zero-damage debuff turn to set up Inferno so self-damage and Hemokinesis add free damage, then kill the 67 HP ship quickly while blocking its 12-13 hits.
Block through Jet turns, stay above the safe HP line, and use the no-attack Pressurize turn plus vulnerable setup to burst the clam down, keeping the fight short.
The self-damage engine is the only scaling: get it online early, then block the big hits and grind 221 HP down; clear Beckons rather than over-drawing so unblockable end-of-turn damage never stacks.

Start the Inferno engine so each self-damage triggers 6 AOE on both bugs, then focus the rock bug down first, blocking its Headbutt to earn the stun, and finish the nectar bug before it starts Thrashing 18.
Kill in about four turns: full damage every turn even into Burrow's block, use the no-attack burrow turn to unload, block enough on BELOW turns to keep HP near target.
Use the free first turn to bring the self-damage engine online; afterwards push 25+ damage per turn, block the Puncture and Bite turns, and end it in about five turns rather than trading HP.
Bring the cheap self-damage AOE engine online early, then clear the swarm fast, finishing the weakest bugs so fewer attackers remain, while blocking enough to keep HP safe for the act boss.
End it in ~3-4 turns: focus the Myte whose next move is Bite, let AOE/self-damage hit both, kill the second right after, and stay near the 90% crab line.

Spread damage evenly across all three segments each turn, win the clock with AOE and the self-damage engine, and bring all three low so they die in the same turn — no single-target focus, a little HP loss is fine.
Focus one Chomper first to halve incoming Clamp damage; the self-damage engine turns each HP loss into 6 AOE on both, so block Clamp turns and end within ~4 turns.
Run the self-damage AOE engine early, then maximum damage each turn keeping both claws HP-aligned for a same-turn double kill; heaviest incoming is the T3 Bug Sting and T4 Laser 41-49.
Deck has no scaling or AOE, so end this in about three turns: damage over defense, accept a few points of HP loss, but avoid dropping far below the 85% boss-entry pace this early.
End this hallway fight quickly: remove the shrinking beetle first so our damage is not cut, then finish the buffing worm. Full HP makes trading damage acceptable.

Kill the parasite quickly, then focus the wormlings down one at a time while blocking only the survivors — never turtle, since each worm scales and adds Infections. Keep enough HP for the boss six floors away.

Use the free stun turn for full damage, then delete wormlings one at a time, lowest HP first, to cut attacker count. Block only real incoming; finish before their Strength and Infections stack, since the act boss is six floors away.
54 HP and no scaling cards, so this should end in about three turns. Remove the buffing nibbit first to cut incoming, then the other; frontload damage, blocking only against the big hits.
Use the two free opening turns for full frontload to cross 150 HP and trigger the stun; then block the plow/Crush turns, attack on zero-incoming turns, and finish fast — no scaling in deck.
Pure race: frontload maximum damage every turn to kill 84 HP before the escape timer runs out. Block only lethal or near-lethal incoming; accept small HP loss to keep damage flowing.
Preserve HP: block first, fully blocking the rock when cheap to trigger its stun for a free turn; kill the egg first so only one attacker remains, then finish the rock.
Focus one bug down at a time so fewer attackers hit us; accept modest HP loss for damage and block only the heavy hits. Multi-hit or 9-damage attacks beat big hits wasted on the cap.
End this fast: remove the Myte that bites next, then the other, blocking only the bites that would land. Accept small HP loss to shorten the fight — fewer attackers alive is the real defence here.
Race the toad: frontload the free buff turn, kill in about four turns, blocking only enough to survive the 23 spike turn; favour single heavy hits because thorns 5 punishes multi-hit cards.

Use the sleep window to kill rock then silk, avoiding wasted damage into the beetle's 18 plating; block the headbutt fully when it triggers the stun; once the beetle wakes, apply vulnerable and burst it down while keeping HP near 55+ for t…

Full damage weight from the start: use the free curse turn to develop, then apply Vulnerable early and burst with multi-hits so the 30-HP heal cycle never outpaces us; block the big attack turns enough to stay alive.
Single 47 HP enemy: end it in about three turns with full damage. Accept small chip damage but do not fall under roughly half HP, since act 1 boss still needs a healthy entry.
Single 42 HP hallway enemy: end it in about three turns with full damage, blocking only the heavier Slam turns; no need to trade extra HP since it buffs over time.
Kill it in about three turns. Block the 16 per turn just enough to stay safe, use recurring AOE and attacks; don't let it stack buffs or steal gold.
Short fight against a non-scaling enemy that outlasts us: keep full damage pressure, block only enough to avoid a second clean hit, and finish before chip damage and status cards stack up.
Single non-minion foe: end it in about four turns with full damage, but don't pour chip hits into Plating. Block only the Jet turns enough to stay comfortable for the boss.
Single 60 HP construct, no scaling: end it in about 3 turns with full damage while blocking each punch enough to stay healthy for the act boss.
Kill all three rats fast, focus fire so fewest attackers remain, use AOE. Block just enough to limit HP loss; a rest site follows before the Soul Fysh boss.
Use the early turns for permanent Strength, then deal maximum damage every turn; block the large hits, spend spare energy clearing Beckons, and use potions this fight since this is the boss.
End it fast: spread damage evenly across all three so the 9-per-hit cap is not wasted, block the incoming hits, and remove the scaling buffer first.
End it in about three or four turns: full damage through the burrow block instead of pure defending, block only what is cheap, so the steady 23s never grind us down.
During the beetle's sleep, kill both bowlbugs, rock first; then apply Vulnerable and burst the beetle before its roll-outs scale — end it fast, accepting a little more chip damage.
Survive: block first, damage second, all damage into Obscura. Hit the Parafright only in a turn it dies outright, since it returns at full HP next turn and split damage is wasted.
Lone 48 HP monster, roughly a 3-turn fight. Take the fast damage line, block only what is cheap, and protect HP for the coming boss.
Burn the mushroom down before adds pile up: damage first, only the block needed to survive, area damage when minions stack, then finish the main body.
Develop permanent Strength and chip through Slippery with multi-hit attacks; block heavily on the big DISMEMBER turns and keep potions for emergencies; win before the Strength loop outgrows us.
Single weak enemy: end it in a few turns with maximum damage, blocking only the incoming kicks so HP stays near 90% for Soul Fysh; no potions worth spending here.
One 67 HP normal enemy: push damage every turn, stacking vulnerability early so Molten Fist and Bash hit harder, and block only the 12-13 attack turns so the fight ends before status cards pile up.
Short fight: remove the buffing cultist first, then the Seapunk, blocking their 11-20 combined each turn. Trade only a little HP for damage, stay near half HP, and keep the potion for the act boss.
Focus one slug down fast: each kill also stuns the survivors for a free turn, so chain kills. Take the debuffer first to avoid Weak, block only against big hits, and keep HP for the act boss.
Single 82 HP enemy that does not scale: push maximum damage each turn and finish within about three turns; small HP loss is fine, keep both potions for the act boss four floors away.
Single 54 HP enemy that grows on unblocked hits: race it down in ~4 turns, blocking enough to prevent unblocked damage; keep HP and potions intact for the forced Elite and Soul Fysh boss.
Free buff turn: dump damage now. Kill the harder-hitting 39 HP cultist first, then the 53 HP one; once they attack, block the ~17/turn while finishing fast.
Race the 221 HP boss: keep damage high every turn, block the heavy hits, spend spare energy removing the added status cards, and avoid wasting damage during Intangible.
Single 92 HP enemy, no growth: pour damage from turn one, break the burrow block the turn it lands, then finish; block just enough to stay above 90% for the crab.

Focus-fire one bug at a time (biggest attacker first) so fewer enemies are alive each turn; accept small chip while blocking the 8-hit. No AOE here, so single-target damage is the whole fight; keep HP for the crab boss.
Race the elite: keep all three segments' HP close and finish them inside one window, since lone kills just revive. Block the multi-hits; let Strength growth and doubled Vulnerable carry damage.
End it in about five turns at ~33 damage per turn: hit every turn, but cover the big Bees/Spear turns so HP stays safe for the forced elite run into the Crab boss.
Short two-enemy fight: race it down, killing the buffing toadpole first, using multi-hit/AOE to hit both. Block only the larger incoming turns; do not let it drag on as spike damage escalates.

One 54 HP normal that grows stronger whenever it lands unblocked damage. Burst it down with vulnerable-boosted multi-hits in about three turns, blocking its hits to cap its Strength, and keep enough HP for the boss ahead.
Kill the pack fast: AOE plus focused damage to remove one rat at a time, the summoner/debuffer first; block only when no kill is available, since fewer attackers is the defence.
Frontload damage to cross half HP fast: the stun and Terror turns are free, so bank attacks then. Hold enough block for the 22/33 hits and finish before Vulnerable grinding kills us.
Hold 20 HP: block the attack turns, take the buff turn for maximum damage, and kill the clam within a few turns while spending almost no HP. Potions stay for the boss.
Remove the 40 HP cultist immediately before its ritual buff, then finish the seapunk with focused damage while keeping enough block to stay near the 85% HP mark for the Waterfall Giant.
Damage first on its buff and non-attack turns, block Pressure Gun and STOMP, finish it before stacks and heals pile up; enter the death turn with HP above the eruption stacks.

Two attackers, one of them scaling: remove the nectar bug first since it is cheaper to kill and grows to 18 hits, let AOE clip both, and take free full-blocks that stun the rock to save HP for the boss.
One 92 HP hallway target: frontload damage and break the Burrow block the turn it lands, ending the fight in about three turns rather than grinding behind block.
End it fast with multi-hit and AOE so the 9-damage cap costs nothing; focus one bug at a time so fewer attackers remain. Small HP loss is fine; save potions for the act boss.
All damage on The Obscura from the summon turn; ~30/turn ends it in ~4–5 turns and the Parafright leaves with it. Block both attackers; only finish the Parafright in one blow if HP drops very low.

Use the 3-turn sleep window: kill the two bowl bugs first (Rock, then Silk), ignoring the sleeping beetle's plating; then burst the woken beetle with vulnerable and multi-hits before its rolls outscale us.
Frontload attack damage and keep skill plays minimal; roughly 35 damage per turn ends its 171 HP in about five turns, well above the 70% entry HP line.
Race the summon: all damage on the Ovicopter body — its eggs and minions vanish when it dies. Use the free summon turn for damage, block the SMASH turns, keep HP for the elite and crab boss.
Block first, kill only with spare energy: at 26 HP every swarm must be covered, Dazed build-up is the real clock, and Lizard Tail is a one-time safety net, not a resource to spend.
Hold both claws' HP even so they die in one turn; block the 41-49 laser and Crusher hits; take Strength/energy early, then apply AOE and attacks every turn.
Single low-HP monster: deal damage every turn to end it fast, taking only cheap blocks when a hit would otherwise chip us meaningfully; keep HP high for the coming act-1 route.
Use the free debuff turn to hit hard, then end the 41 HP beetle in a few turns while blocking the 7-13 hits; HP stays above the 90% boss target.
Focus single-target damage on Flyconid, use the slime's status turn for a free AOE/burst window, block only the incoming 11, and close the fight in ~3-4 turns while keeping HP for the act boss.
Deck has no powers or permanent Strength, so end the 76 HP Mawler quickly: full damage each turn, blocking just enough to stay safe, and avoid dragging the fight into buffed claws.
普通走廊战,两敌都会成长。用AOE同时压下血量,单体优先秒掉贾克斯果断其增益,再收飞蝇菌子;速战速决,少付血,下个节点是休息点,不需要为这场留药水。

No scaling enemies and the deck has three AOE cards, so end this within two or three turns: sweep the small slimes with AOE, focus single-target damage on the twig medium first, block only the biggest incoming hit and accept minor chip dam…

Killing the priest ends the fight, so single-target damage stays on it; AOE incidentally whittles followers, which only matter if one threatens a kill. Deck has no strength, so push damage every turn and finish near T9 before ritual beams …
Basic deck with no AoE: focus one toadpole down at a time, block the incoming hits, and close the fight fast before thorns and chip damage stack up.
Weak single hallway enemy, 42 HP. Block the 8-12 hits, chip it down with attacks and Bash, avoid unnecessary chip damage: HP 54/86 is under the boss-prep target and a shop is next.
Push 15+ damage per turn to beat the 9 Plating, use the no-attack PRESSURIZE turn as a burst window, block the JET hits enough to end it in about four turns.
Kill slugs one at a time: every kill stuns the survivors and cancels their turn, so kills are defence. Block the residual damage and finish clustered low-HP slugs together.

Kill within ~4 turns: block its hits to deny SUCK_POWER Strength, take permanent Strength/Plating early for lasting value, then push damage. Keep HP near 85% for the matriarch boss after the rest site.
Sleep turns are free setup: build Strength and block, keep its HP untouched so it stays asleep. Once awake, full damage while blocking the big hits; kill before Soul Siphon drains stats.
~4 turns to deal 84 before it flees with a stolen card, so weight every turn to damage; early Strength powers are fine but blocking only covers the 17/21 hits needed to stay safe for the crab.
End this in about four turns: spread AOE and multi-hit damage to cut attackers down, accept a little HP loss but stay near the 90% boss entry target.
Set up permanent Strength early while only one Chomper attacks, then kill them one at a time, blocking the 8x2 clamps; accept some HP loss now for a much faster finish and less deck clogging.
Use the sleep turns to land permanent Strength and thin the two bowlbugs (rock first), then turn vulnerable plus multi-hit damage on the beetle and fight behind enough block to stop each big hit.
Kill the Myte whose next move is Bite first, then the other; halving incoming is the defence. Keep blocking most turns and do not let the fight drag — their Strength climbs every cycle.

Use the debuff turn (no incoming damage) to frontload everything and end this 42 HP beetle in about two turns; block the 13-damage STOMP hits, but don't trade extra HP for nothing since the boss wants ~90% entry.
Frontload into Flyconid while AoE chips Jaxfruit; end it in a few turns so Frail and buffs don't stack, keeping HP for the Kin boss.
Focus all damage on Fogmog; its summons vanish when it dies, so ignore them except incidental AoE. Block its hits, keep HP high, spend no reserved potions.
Frontload damage into Flyconid first so the spores stop, letting AoE chip the slime; end the fight in about four turns while blocking the worst hits, keeping HP in reserve for The Kin.
End this in a few turns before hounds join: burst the Tracker first, then the Assassin, leave the Axe last. AoE chips all three; block enough to blunt the 10 and 5 hits, accept small HP loss.
Race the priest: all single-target damage on it, AoE only splashes followers. Block the beam/orb turns, keep HP above ~21, and end it before the T11 Beam; hold reserved potions.
Deck is damage-starved and this punk is only 48 HP: apply Vulnerable and frontload attacks to finish in about three turns, blocking only what is cheap, then recover with Burning Blood.
Short two-enemy fight: race them down with AOE plus single-target damage, killing the buffing one before its buff compounds, spending only enough block to limit chip damage.
Clear this trio quickly with AOE and Vulnerable so total incoming drops fast; each kill stuns the survivors, but expect the last slug to gain Strength. Avoid extra chip on our 60 HP before the boss.

Focus one gardener down at a time so incoming drops each turn, using AOE and Vulnerable early; block just enough to keep HP near full for the elite-heavy path and the Matriarch, saving the forge potion for her wake-up burst.
Race it down in 2-3 turns: Vulnerable plus heavy attacks and AOE frontload, blocking only when it fully prevents damage so Suck never stacks; keep HP high for the Matriarch.

Sleep turns: cycle/draw, don't touch its HP; once awake race — stack Vulnerable, then all damage, blocking only to survive each hit. Soul Siphon cuts our block every cycle, so it must die before ~10 turns.
Use the no-attack debuff turn for damage, block only the bigger hits, and kill the 41 HP beetle quickly so repeated Shrinks don't drag the fight and cost more HP.
Kill the buffing fruit first (lowest HP, feeds the fungus), then the fungus. Block the 11-13 hits where cheap, scale early, and finish fast so HP is kept for the act boss.
Near-full HP and a one-turn sleep window: spend it on damage and kill before Strength-boosted 23 Slashes grind us down. A little HP loss is fine; losing this race is not.
Low-HP swarm at full HP: clear the 12-HP Inklet first, then 16 and 18, trading minimal HP. Boss is 5 floors away on preserve policy, so stay efficient and don't overspend block.
Three raiders, 68 total HP. First turn is safe (10 incoming): establish AOE/strength, then kill Assassin, Crossbow before FIRE, Tracker last. Stay near full HP for the boss.
Enemy buffs before attacking: use the free setup turn for scaling powers, then kill fast with strength and vulnerable. Block the big hits, keep HP near the 68 boss-entry target.
Small 98-HP hallway before a forced rest: remove the Shrinker Beetle first so its damage-reducing debuff and stomp stop, then finish the crawler fast, blocking only what keeps us near boss-entry HP.

Use the two free opening turns for permanent scaling, then push damage to stun it below 150. Afterwards block the big plows, survive Ringing turns with one-card block, and hold potions for those spikes.
Remove the Nectar before its buff becomes 18-damage turns, fully block the Rock's headbutt to farm stuns, then clean up the Rock. Trade a little HP for speed, but stay above the 85% entry target.
Long capped-damage fight: ramp permanent Strength/block engines early and let AOE chip all three, then kill one bug at a time to cut incoming; keep HP near boss entry level.
Outlast it: block Puncture and Bite almost fully, grind its 126 HP down with permanent scaling and self-damage AoE, keeping HP for the Knowledge Demon nine floors away.

Scale first: play powers early to build permanent Strength and AOE damage across all segments, block the combined attacks, then kill all three segments in one turn; keep the reserved potion for the boss.

Curse turns give free windows: land permanent Strength and self-damage engines early, ramp Rainbow Ring and Rupture, then convert into Vulnerable burst and multi-hit damage. Block the Slap and Overwhelming turns; never let the heal cycle e…

End it in about three turns: AOE and multi-hit to clear both slugs together, finishing the lower-HP one first so the survivor's stun cancels an attack; block the remaining hits rather than trading HP needlessly.
Kill fast: all damage concentrated on one gardener until it dies, AOE softening the rest; their incoming grows after Enlarge, so trading a little HP to remove attackers quickly is worth it.

Now is the damage window: only 11 incoming this turn. Use AOE to hit both, kill the buffing cultist first to stop its scaling, then finish the Seapunk — end it in 3-4 turns, keeping HP near full for the boss.
Short single-enemy fight: end it in about three turns, using the free READY turn for damage or setup, without spending potions or over-blocking so HP stays high for the boss.
Single 54 HP enemy that grows stronger on unblocked damage: end it in about three turns with committed damage, keeping chips blocked so Strength never stacks and boss HP stays near 85%.
End the 53 HP merc in 2-3 turns: full damage from multi-hit and AOE, blocking the double smashes enough to reach the rest site healthy. Killing fast stops the buff compounding.

Race the eruption clock: maximum damage every turn, stacking strength for Whirlwind/Stomp/Howl, while fully blocking Pressure Gun and Stomp and keeping HP above the eruption stacks; kill as early as possible.
Race the crawler down in a few turns: Bash/Uppercut frontload, block only the big hit turns, end before Inhale stacks make its attacks too costly.
Spread AOE to bring all three down together, focus the Brute first so it stops buffing the group, then the Crossbow; block enough to survive the combined attack while out-damaging them.
Punish the no-damage INFECT turn with maximum frontload, kill the parasite, then AOE the worms together and finish each one; block only the real LASH hits, never a full block turn.
Free stun turn: dump maximum frontload. Then focus the lowest-HP worm first, one at a time, using AOE to soften the rest, blocking only the real bite turns; never a full block turn.
Use the free sleeping turn for maximum frontload and kill this elite fast: apply Weak/Vulnerable early, accept minor HP loss if it ends the fight before the +10 Strength slashes stack up.
Single 70-HP construct that charges now then escalates. Kill in about 3 turns, blocking its big attack turns, and keep enough HP for the boss three floors away.
End this quickly: strip Slippery with AOE, then bring all three down together so incoming damage stops sooner. Keep enough HP for the boss in two floors and the rest site ahead.
Use the two free Buff turns to set up the Rupture+ strength engine; self-damage grows it. Race below 150 for the stun, block Plow/Crush turns, and finish with AOE once Strength is high.
Short two-enemy fight: bring the rock down first since the egg will hide behind block; make the headbutt turn fully blocked to earn a stun, and let multi-target damage finish the egg.
Clear all three bugs fast with AOE and multi-hit damage, killing the buffing one first; block just enough to survive the ramp and end this within a few turns.
Race the Ovicopter: concentrate all damage on the body so it dies before eggs pile up. Block enough to survive the 19 smash, and keep HP for the act boss.
Unload Hemokinesis, Molten Fist and Bash-backed strikes to close the 47 HP in about two turns; block only with leftover energy, keep potions unused and HP loss small ahead of the Matriarch.

Single 58 HP enemy that regains decaying Plating each turn and buffs Strength every other turn. Chew through the Plating consistently and close the fight in a few turns; block the JET turns enough to enter the boss layer near 85% HP.
Single 51 HP thief: kill within ~3 turns so it cannot keep stealing gold or stack its HEHE buff. Frontload damage; block only enough to survive a following 16-hit swing.
Frontload vulnerable-boosted burst (Bash into Molten Fist/Dismantle/Hemokinesis) and end it in ~3 turns before status cards pile up; block the small hits, stay healthy for the F15 elite.
Frontload vulnerable-backed damage to race it down; push below 75 to trigger the stun, exploit that free turn, keep block for buffed CRASH hits; hold the attack potion for the boss.

Use the three sleep turns as free setup without waking it, then race: maximum frontload damage every turn before Soul Siphon drains our Strength and Dexterity and its HP and Plating outlast our 80 HP.
Short hallway: cull the attackers quickly so incoming shrinks, spread AOE chip on all three, block the larger hits. Hold HP near 72 for the act-2 boss; no potions in stock.
Race it down: 84 HP with Bash+/Molten Fist/Dismantle/Hemokinesis frontload should die in ~3 turns. Block only the 17s that threaten the boss-prep HP bank; never let it reach its escape.

Spend a bit of HP to frontload vulnerable-boosted burst and self-damage triggers, killing it before its repeated Strength gains make Pounce lethal; block only to avoid Frail-heavy chip turns, not to grind.

Block each alternating 16 fully; at 27 HP no unblocked swing. Damage only from safety, focus one Chomper to halve incoming, then finish the second; AOE/self-damage engine carries; bank HP for the Crab.
End the hallway quickly with big frontloaded hits; block only enough to stay safe, since each card played under Tender weakens later cards; keep boss potions reserved.
Use the free buff turn to frontload maximum damage, block the 23 and 17 hits, favour single-hit attacks while thorns are up, and close before a second spike cycle.
All damage at The Obscura while blocking the combined incoming; only spend a turn killing the Parafright when it can die in one turn, otherwise ignore it and out-race the pair.
Spend the early turns setting up the self-damage AOE engine and Strength while blocking the big hits, keep both claws' HP even, then kill both in one turn.

Single 59 HP crawler with a Strength buff — use the deck's frontload (Twin Strike/Bash/Headbutt) to end it in about 4 turns, blocking only enough to avoid real HP loss, since run policy keeps HP high for the boss.
Focus all damage on the Flyconid first to stop the frail/vulnerable spores and cut incoming damage, then finish the buffing Jaxfruit; block just enough to keep HP near 85% for the act boss.
Four slimes at 92 HP total, only two weak pokes incoming now but ~26 next turn. Kill the 12 and 16 HP slimes first to cut attacker count, then the mediums; keep HP high for the forced F13 elite.
Deploy powers/plating now while the parasite infects instead of attacking, then kill it fast and focus each spawned worm one at a time; keep HP for the boss four floors away.
Use the stun turn for maximum damage, then focus and kill worms one at a time (lowest HP first) so incoming drops fast; block only what is needed and keep HP for the boss four floors away.
Short brawl: drop attackers one at a time, Assassin then Tracker, Brute last; burst now beats turtling since only ~79 HP total and a rest site follows.
